title: Showcase: the by-ear tune
summary: A mini recital: the written piece, plus the tune you picked out by ear, names said and one question.
materials: the piece from your teacher, with a pencil

figure.alt: Two boxes stacked, one for the written piece and one for the four bars of the tune picked out by ear, the two pieces named on the recital card.

steps.title: Showcase: the by-ear tune
steps.body:
This recital has two pieces: the written piece, and the four bars you found by ear.

1. Choose the written piece, and write both names on a card, the by-ear tune second.
2. Run the written piece once a day, hard bars first.
3. Run the by-ear tune once a day too, checking it still matches the tune in your head.
4. On recital day, say each name out loud, play both, and hold the last note of the written piece.
5. Bow. The family asks one question, and you decide whether to answer about the written piece or the by-ear tune.

Playing something you found yourself, in front of people, is its own kind of proof. The tune lives in your ears now, not only on a page.

figure.alt: Two boxes stacked, the written piece and the by-ear tune, each run once a day before recital day, names said out loud for both.

steps.title: Recital checklist
steps.body: Tick each one before recital day.
checklist: Written piece and the by-ear tune chosen, names written on a card
Written piece run once a day, hard bars first
The by-ear tune run once a day, checked against the tune in your head
Names said out loud before each piece, a bow at the end
The family asked one question, and you answered it

steps.title: Record the recital
steps.prompt: Record both pieces in one take, names said out loud, phone where it sees the hands. Slips stay in.
